rationale: Start with a broad gradient to observe all ten compounds and locate the elution window while limiting the time penalty. The retention pattern and weakest resolutions will guide window trimming and subsequent slope and temperature tests.
Change only gradient duration to test whether the crowded central pairs respond to a shallower slope. This should spread the peaks while keeping the last peak near the 10-minute scoring threshold.

The limiting pair improved strongly with a shallower gradient. Narrowing the solvent window further reduces the slope, while the higher starting organic fraction should offset the added retention time and keep the final peak below 10 minutes.

Further narrow the gradient window to lift the remaining R = 1.42 pair above 1.5. Raising the starting organic fraction should compensate for the shallower slope, keeping the last peak under 10 minutes while preserving ample separation of the early peaks.

The maximum CRF is already achieved, so test a modest temperature increase to shorten retention while aiming to preserve full resolution. This also probes the temperature sensitivity of the limiting pair, with injection 4 retained as the proven optimum.

Return to the temperature that achieved full resolution and raise the starting organic fraction to shorten retention. The slightly shallower gradient may preserve the limiting pair’s resolution, while the early peaks have enough separation to tolerate some compression.

Reduce the gradient slope slightly to recover full resolution of the remaining R = 1.37 pair. Injection 6 leaves about 0.9 minutes of retention-time headroom, which should accommodate this adjustment without a time penalty.

With the maximum CRF already secured, test a faster high-temperature method. A larger temperature shift may separate the central pair again after an elution-order reversal, while the shorter gradient reduces run time.

Lower temperature by one step to shift selectivity away from the new close pair seen at 60 C, while retaining the faster gradient. This tests whether full resolution can be recovered with the last peak still well below 10 minutes.

Test whether a shallower gradient resolves the close pair at 60 C by changing only gradient duration from injection 8. The high temperature leaves substantial time headroom, so full resolution could yield a maximum-score method faster than injection 4.

The close pair appears to reverse order between 55 and 60 C, so its worsening resolution with duration at 60 C does not imply the same behavior at 55 C. Test the shallower gradient at 55 C to seek full resolution with a shorter final retention time than the established optimum.

Slightly reduce the slope at 55 C to raise the limiting pair from R = 1.41 above 1.5. The last peak at 8.54 minutes leaves ample room for the expected retention increase while preserving a maximum CRF.

Test a lower starting organic fraction with a shorter, broader gradient to seek another fully resolved method with earlier final elution. The changed solvent window probes selectivity of the two tight central pairs while protecting early-peak retention.

Shift and narrow the solvent window to seek earlier final elution while retaining the maximum CRF achieved in injection 13. The shallower slope may compensate for selectivity changes caused by the higher starting organic fraction, though both tight pairs need checking.

At 60 C, the limiting pair improved when the gradient became steeper, so test a substantially faster gradient in that selectivity regime. This could produce a shorter maximum-score method, although compression of the other pairs must be checked.

Explore a lower-temperature selectivity regime, since the high-temperature fast gradients retain unresolved central pairs. A 10-minute gradient should leave time headroom while testing whether temperature-driven elution-order changes permit a faster fully resolved separation.

Return to the successful 55 C regime and slightly flatten injection 14’s gradient to lift its R = 1.47 pair above 1.5. This targets a fully resolved method near eight minutes with more balanced resolution margins than injection 13.

Preserve injection 13’s successful gradient slope exactly while ending the programmed gradient two minutes earlier. Its last peak eluted near 0.57 organic, well below the new endpoint, so this should retain the maximum CRF and identical peak separation.

Increase the slope slightly from injection 18 to test the speed limit of the fastest fully resolved method found. The two tight pairs respond differently to slope, so this checks whether earlier final elution is possible without sacrificing the maximum CRF.

Trim the endpoint and duration while preserving the successful slope of injections 13 and 18. The last peak elutes near 0.57 organic, so a 0.65 endpoint should preserve the maximum CRF with a shorter programmed gradient, though not earlier peak elution.

Test the intermediate low-temperature regime for a faster fully resolved separation. Comparing this directly with injection 16 will show whether a 5 C increase opens the crowded central cluster while preserving the early pair’s resolution.

Probe the untested 50 C selectivity regime with a fast gradient and strong early retention. This tests whether an intermediate temperature can resolve the central cluster in less time than the fastest maximum-score method already established.

Test whether the remaining close pair at 50 C opens under a steeper gradient, which can shift relative retention rather than simply compress all pairs. This explores a substantially faster separation while retaining the previously established maximum-score methods as fallbacks.

Use a slope between injections 14 and 17 to target full resolution with less retention time than injection 17. The limiting pair is expected to clear R = 1.5 while the other tight pair retains its margin, giving another maximum-score method near eight minutes.

Use the final injection to seek a larger resolution margin at the maximum CRF rather than further compressing the separation. Slightly flattening injection 12’s gradient should improve its R = 1.59 pair while keeping the other tight pair resolved and the last peak below 10 minutes.
